parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem:
The p$K_a$ values for stage 1 and stage 2 for some dicarboxylic acids are listed below.

| $n$ in $\text{HO}_2\text{C(CH}_2\text{)}_n\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ | p$K_a$(1) for stage 1 | p$K_a$(2) for stage 2 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | 2.83 | 5.69 |
| 2 | 4.16 | 5.61 |
| 3 | 4.31 | 5.41 |

For comparison, the p$K_a$ of ethanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, is 4.76.
parts.text: State the mathematical relationship between p$K_a$ and the acid dissociation constant $K_a$.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
With reference to the table above, suggest why the p$K_a$(1) values

- are all smaller than the p$K_a$ of ethanoic acid,

- become larger as n increases.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: Suggest why all the p$K_a$(2) values in the table above are larger than the p$K_a$ of ethanoic acid.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: The monosodium salts of edible dicarboxylic acids are added to some foodstuffs as buffers.
parts.text: Explain what is meant by the term *buffer solution*.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Write two equations to show how monosodium butanedioate, $\text{HO}_2\text{CCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{Na}$, acts as a buffer.
